title: docs(spec,skills): SkillSchema.tools decides whether an MCP server offers the skill
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoApmMR185WHiVqD18d3QHhx)_

Fixes #32885

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：已发布文字不再把技能的 `tools` 绑定写成「开源版无效」，也不再说「带 instructions 的技能对任何连接都提供」：spec 的 `skill.zod.ts`（类注释、`tools` 注释与它的 describe 文案，连带再生的参考页）、`content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`、`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`，以及席位追加的四处：`content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`、`packages/mcp/README.md`、`packages/spec/liveness/skill.json` 的 `tools` 条目、`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` 的一处注释。现在都写明：`registerSkillPrompts` 安装的 MCP 提示面，只有在该服务器列出技能绑定的每一个工具时，才在 `prompts/list` / `prompts/get` 提供这个技能。
- 为什么改：这条收窄已随 18.4.0 发布（PR #32880），文字却还说绑定无效。照旧文写技能的人或 AI 会给技能绑上 MCP 不提供的工具，技能就在连接上不出现，而文档里找不到原因。
- 风险与回滚：只改注释、describe 文案、文档和技能文字；schema 形状、接受集、运行行为都不变。回滚即 revert。`objectstack-ai` 技能 5813 → 5929 token（上限 6801）。
- 先看：① `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts` 里 `tools` 的注释和 describe（规则全文在这里）；② `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` 内置技能表下面那一段；③ `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` 的「A skill is offered only where its tools are」一段（含 `actions:execute` 的例子）。
- 两分钟验证：`git grep -n "runtime only" content/docs/references/ai/skill.mdx`，预期只剩 `surface` 和 `triggerConditions` 两行，`tools` 行不再出现。
- 需要你做的：席位契约复审通过后批准本 PR（`skills/**` 属 Tier H）。

## What changes

The rule is written from PR #32880's changeset and from `registerSkillPrompts` in `packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts` on `main` 588596af, not from the card's summary (card comment 6840247483):

> the exported `registerSkillPrompts(server, bridge)` offers a skill on `prompts/list` and `prompts/get` only when the server it is installed on lists every tool in the skill's binding, read from that server's own tool registry when the prompt request is answered

- **`packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts`**
  - Class JSDoc, "Where each half of a skill runs": `instructions` runs in both distributions, and where `registerSkillPrompts` installs the prompt surface the skill is offered only on a server that serves every tool it binds. `tools` is bound by the cloud runtime and read by MCP. `surface` and `triggerConditions` stay cloud-runtime-only and inert in the open framework.
  - `tools` JSDoc: the last paragraph states the rule. A plain name is served by a tool of that name, a trailing wildcard by any listed tool it matches, and an `action_NAME` entry (or `action_*`) also by `run_action` (`bindingEntryServed` reads the literal or wildcard match first, then the `action_` family door). A skill that binds no tool is offered as before, and `prompts/get` answers a withheld skill as it answers a prompt name no skill derives. The reach is `MCPServerRuntime`'s HTTP door and any host that drives its own `McpServer` and calls `registerSkillPrompts`, stdio included; `MCPServerRuntime.bridgePrompts`, which projects skills onto the long-lived server without it, applies no filter.
  - `tools` describe text: "bound by the cloud agent runtime only" becomes "bound by the cloud agent runtime; an MCP server whose prompts `registerSkillPrompts` installs offers the skill only when it serves every tool named here (an `action_` entry also through `run_action`)". No tracker number in it.
  - Regenerated: `content/docs/references/ai/skill.mdx` (the `tools` row). `check:generated` found only that artifact stale.
- **`content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`**: the two rows of the two-halves table, and one paragraph under it that states the rule and the advice that follows (bind a skill only to tools its intended connections serve).
- **`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`**: the note under the built-in skills table. `surface` and `triggerConditions` are inert on the open edition; `tools` binds nothing there but is read, with the rule and which servers apply it.

Added in the rework round, at the seat's order (claim amended, comment 6868603309), the same stale claim in four more files:

- **`content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`**, section "Prompts: your skills, served to the client": the intro no longer says every skill is served; a new paragraph, "A skill is offered only where its tools are", states the rule on the page's own example (`case_triage` binds `query_records` and `action_resolve_case`, so a token without the `actions:execute` scope, which lists no `run_action`, is not offered it); the "Only the instructions half projects" paragraph says `tools` is bound by the in-product runtime and read here only to decide the offer.
- **`packages/mcp/README.md`**, Prompts section: `bridgePrompts` lists every skill that carries instructions on the long-lived server; the HTTP door and any server a host installs `registerSkillPrompts` on apply the rule.
- **`packages/spec/liveness/skill.json`**, `tools` entry: the evidence gains the in-repo reader as a local anchor after the cloud clauses (`packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts#skillBindingServed`), and the note no longer says there is nothing to read server-side. `verifiedAt` and `evidenceScope` are unchanged, because the cloud readers were not re-read. The file note gains one dated sentence.
- **`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`**: one code comment.

Two more sentences changed, both in files the card names and both the same stale claim. The order says to rewrite only the named sentences, so these are declared here and in the report as a deviation:

- `skill.zod.ts`, `instructions` field JSDoc: "a connected client can list this skill by name and fetch this text" gains "on a server that serves the tools the skill binds (see `tools`)".
- `SKILL.md`, `instructions` row: "The one field the open edition reads" becomes "serves". The open edition now reads `tools` as well, so "reads" contradicted the paragraph this PR rewrites.

## Tests

Text only: comments, one describe string, docs and skill prose. No tested behaviour changed, so no ablation. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 840 files, 26832 tests passed (1 todo) at f58d610e; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- Published `skills/**` readings. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`: 421 → 427 lines, 23270 → 23736 bytes, 5813 → 5929 tokens (ceiling 6801, headroom 872). All `SKILL.md` files together: 4595 → 4601 lines, 235154 → 235620 bytes. No ceiling is raised.
- `stack.tools` records are still described as inert in the `tools` JSDoc ("no runtime reader until that lands"). That sentence is about tool records, not about the binding, and is unchanged.
